extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of satirical Renaissance literature (general literate public)
extracted.subtask_description: Authorial prologue and narrative passages that state informal principles about clarity, brevity, style, and readerly taste relevant to composing or judging satirical, vernacular Renaissance prose. Mixes prescriptive remarks with examples and satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems/questions must be certain, clear, and intelligible
rubrics_metrics.description: The Peripatetics have wisely made a rule that all problems, questions, and doubts which are offered to be solved ought to be certain, clear, and intelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rule to filter which questions merit answers; vague or ill-posed problems should be rejected or clarified before answering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answers should be short and avoid pedantic cant
rubrics_metrics.description: My answer shall be short, not to tire you with a long needless train of pedantic cant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor concise responses over long, pedantic exposition. Do not prolong answers with needless scholarly jargon that will weary the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer demonstrative action/signs over ornate words for practical matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The belly has no ears, nor is it to be filled with fair words; you shall be answered to content by signs and gestures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practical or bodily needs (metaphorically: an audience with simple appetite), use visible action, demonstration, or plain provisions rather than rhetorical flourish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor plain, merry, accessible writing over dark, obscure, pedantic works
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole cartloads of books... were tiresome, dull, soporiferous, irksome, mischievous, crabbed, knotty, puzzling, and dark... In their stead beans in cod are started up; that is, these merry and fructifying Pantagruelian books... I have made bold to choose to chirrup and warble my plain ditty... rather than be thought deaf among so many pretty poets and eloquent orators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose in the mother-tongue and a plain, lively style; aim to entertain and be fruitful (merry and accessible) rather than obscure, knotty, or needlessly learned. Avoid imitating incomprehensible scholastic or pedantic writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical schedule for daily life (prescriptive hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians more properly say that the canonical hours are, To rise at five, to dine at nine, To sup at five, to sleep at nine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescriptive timetable is offered as an ideal regimen for bodily health and order; it functions as a model of proper timing/rhythm in life (and by extension in orderly composition or conduct).
